transcript.text: my washin mashine wont turn on at all no lights nothin

When a washing machine is completely dead, with no lights or response at all, the cause is usually that power isn't reaching it rather than the machine itself failing. 1. No power at the socket. The socket may be dead, or there may be a separate switched or fused spur (a switch often on the wall above the worktop or in a nearby cupboard) that's been knocked off.
2. Vibration from spinning can gradually ease a plug out of the socket.
3. A fault inside the machine on the incoming power side. The usual suspects are the mains filter (the first part that gets power) or its wiring, and less often the control board's power supply. 1. Plug something else you know works, such as a kettle or lamp, into the same socket. If it doesn't work either, the problem is the supply, not the washer. Check your consumer unit for a tripped switch.
2. Look for a separate switch for the washing machine and make sure it's on. Many kitchens have one, and it's easy to flick off by mistake. If it's a fused spur, the fuse in it can blow too.
3. Switch off, unplug the machine and check the lead and plug. Look for cuts, crushing where it runs behind the machine, or scorch marks on the plug. Then push the plug firmly back in. If it comes on after reseating, it had simply worked loose.
4. If you have a spare 13A fuse, swap the plug fuse (with the machine unplugged). If it comes back to life, it's worth thinking about why the fuse blew. A one-off can happen, but if it blows again, stop and have it looked at rather than keep replacing fuses. If you notice any burning smell or scorch marks, or you heard a bang before it died, leave it unplugged. If the socket, switch, plug and fuse all check out and it's still completely dead, the fault is inside the machine. The mains filter or its wiring would be the first thing to look at, ahead of the control board. To start: does another appliance work in that same socket, and is there a separate switch for the washing machine that's turned on?
the kettle works in the other sockets, but i cant reach the plug for the washin mashine its behind the unit. not sure about a seperate switch, il have a look

That's a useful start. Because the kettle works in other sockets, your house supply is fine, but the washing machine's own socket hasn't been tested yet. When a plug is hidden behind a unit, it's very often fed through its own switch and fuse, so power can be off just for the machine while everything else works. 1. 2. 3. Less likely, a fault inside the machine where the power comes in. 1. Look for a switch on the wall above the worktop, beside the units or inside a nearby cupboard. It's sometimes labelled "washing machine" or "appliance", and there's often a row of them with one each for the dishwasher, fridge and so on. If one is off, switch it on. If it has a red light that won't come on even with the switch on, the fuse in that switch has probably blown. That points to the supply, not the machine.
2. Check your consumer unit (fuse box) for any switch that has dropped down. Kitchen appliances are sometimes on a separate circuit from the sockets where the kettle worked.
3. If the switch is on and nothing has tripped, the next step is to get at the plug. Switch off at the wall switch first, then ease the machine forward a little at a time. It's heavy, and the hoses and lead are short, so don't yank it. Push the plug firmly in, or test that socket with the kettle. The first suspect is the part where the mains power comes in (the mains filter) or its wiring, rather than the main control board. Let me know what you find with the switch.
ok i looked and theres a row of switches above the worktop, one says washer and its OFF. my flatmate must of switched it off when cleaning. should i turn it back on?

Yes, switch it back on. That's exactly what those switches are for, and it's safe to do. 1. Flick the switch labelled washer to on. If it has a small red indicator light, that should now glow.
2. Press the washing machine's power or on button (or turn the dial off a programme and back on). If the lights and display come on, that was the cause and you're sorted. Run a short programme to make sure it fills and starts normally.
3. If the switch is on but its indicator stays dark and the machine is still dead, the fuse inside that switch has probably blown. A blown fuse is usually a sign of something else, so it's worth knowing why it went. Let me know before we go further. If the switch light comes on but the machine still shows nothing, the next step is checking that the plug behind the unit is pushed fully in. After that, the fault would be on the machine's incoming power side, most likely the mains filter or its wiring. You might also ask your flatmate to leave that switch on, or pop a small note on it, so it doesn't catch you out again. Does it come on now?
ok i turned it back on and the machine lights up now and works! thanks

Nothing was wrong with the machine. Its wall switch had simply been turned off, which happens a lot when people are wiping down worktops. To stop it catching you out again, pop a small label or a bit of tape on that switch saying "leave on", and mention it to your flatmate. Is there anything else I can help with?
